newsitem.title: CHINA: S. Korea seen to invest $3.0 bln in China in 1996.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea seen to invest $3.0 bln in China in 1996.

text.p: A Chinese vice minister has urged South Korean businessmen to invest more in China's less developed central and western regions, the International Business Daily said on Thursday.
Vice Foreign Trade Minister Liu Shan said South Korean businessmen would likely invest $3.0 billion in China in 1996, the newspaper said. He gave no comparative figures.
Two-way trade was expected to hit $20.0 billion this year, Liu said, adding that there was still much potential. He did not give a breakdown for imports and exports.
He told a group of visiting South Korean officials on Wednesday that Seoul should open its markets further to Chinese products, especially agricultural goods.
Liu also urged South Korea to cut tariffs and remove non-tariff barriers.
South Korea enjoyed a surplus of $3.86 billion with China in the first 10 months of 1996, according to Chinese statistics.
